qs.q: The slope of the tangent line to the parametric curve \[ x=t-\sin t,\quad y=1-\cos t \] at the point corresponding to $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is equal to
hints: This is the slope of a tangent line to a parametric curve.
Differentiate $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t$, form the ratio, then substitute the given $t$.
For $x=x(t),\ y=y(t)$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$ when $dx/dt\neq0$.

qs.q: The parametric curve \[ x=4+2\cos t,\quad y=-1+\sin t \] represents
hints: Eliminate the parameter using a trigonometric identity.
Solve for $\cos t$ and $\sin t$ separately, then use the Pythagorean identity.
$\cos^2t+\sin^2t=1$; the curve $\dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2}=1$ is an ellipse (a circle only if $a=b$).
steps: That is $\dfrac{(x-4)^2}{4}+(y+1)^2=1$, with $a=2\neq b=1$, so it is an ellipse.

qs.q: A vector that is orthogonal to both vectors $\vec u=\langle 2,-1,3\rangle$ and $\vec v=\langle 4,5,6\rangle$ is
hints: A vector orthogonal to two vectors comes from the cross product.
Compute $\vec u\times\vec v$ with a determinant; any nonzero multiple of it also works.
$\vec u\times\vec v$ is orthogonal to both $\vec u$ and $\vec v$, and $k\mathbf{w}$ is parallel to $\mathbf{w}$ for $k\neq0$.
steps: $\vec u\times\vec v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\2&-1&3\\4&5&6\end{vmatrix}=(-6-15)\mathbf i-(12-12)\mathbf j+(10+4)\mathbf k$.

qs.q: The projection of $\vec u=\langle4,2,0\rangle$ onto $\vec v=\langle2,1,-1\rangle$ is equal to
hints: This is the vector projection of one vector onto another.
Compute $\vec u\cdot\vec v$ and $\|\vec v\|^2$, then scale $\vec v$.
$\operatorname{proj}_{\vec v}\vec u=\dfrac{\vec u\cdot\vec v}{\|\vec v\|^2}\,\vec v$.

qs.q: The slope of the tangent line to the polar curve $r=\sin\theta$ at the point corresponding to $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is equal to
hints: A polar curve can be treated as a parametric curve with parameter $\theta$.
Write $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$ and form $\dfrac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}$.
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{f'(\theta)\sin\theta+f(\theta)\cos\theta}{f'(\theta)\cos\theta-f(\theta)\sin\theta}$ for $r=f(\theta)$.

qs.q: A vector parallel to the tangent line to the graph of $f(x)=x^2\cos x$ at the point $(\pi,-\pi^2)$ is
hints: The tangent line's direction is determined by its slope.
Find $f'(\pi)$ with the product rule.
A line of slope $m$ is parallel to $\langle1,m\rangle$, and so to every nonzero multiple of it.
steps: A parallel vector is $\langle1,-2\pi\rangle$; its negative is $\langle-1,2\pi\rangle$.

qs.q: If $\langle a,b,c\rangle$ is the vector of magnitude $\dfrac34$ in the opposite direction of the vector $\langle2,-2,1\rangle$, then $a+b+c=$
hints: Use a unit vector in the given direction, reversed and scaled.
Find the length of the given vector, divide to get a unit vector, then multiply by the required signed magnitude.
The unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf w$ is $\dfrac{\mathbf w}{\|\mathbf w\|}$; the opposite direction uses $-\dfrac{\mathbf w}{\|\mathbf w\|}$.

qs.q: An equation for the sphere having the points $(2,1,3)$ and $(1,3,-1)$ as endpoints of a diameter is given by
hints: A sphere is determined by its center and radius.
The center is the midpoint of the diameter; the radius is half the distance between the endpoints.
$(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2+(z-l)^2=r^2$, with center the midpoint of the endpoints and $r$ half the distance between them.

qs.q: The length of the parametric curve \[ x=\sin^{-1}t,\quad y=\ln\sqrt{1-t^2},\quad 0\le t\le\frac14 \] is equal to
hints: This is an arc length of a parametric curve.
Rewrite $y=\frac12\ln(1-t^2)$, differentiate both coordinates, and simplify the sum of squares.
$L=\int_a^b\sqrt{(dx/dt)^2+(dy/dt)^2}\,dt$, and $\int\dfrac{dt}{1-t^2}=\dfrac12\ln\left|\dfrac{1+t}{1-t}\right|+C$.

qs.q: The polar equation $r=\sec\theta-2\cos\theta$, $-\dfrac{\pi}{2}<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, can be converted to the rectangular equation
hints: Convert using $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, $r^2=x^2+y^2$.
Multiply the equation by $r$ so that $r\sec\theta$ and $r\cos\theta$ become expressions in $x$.
$r\cos\theta=x$, $r\sec\theta=\dfrac{r}{\cos\theta}=\dfrac{r^2}{x}$, $r^2=x^2+y^2$.

qs.q: Which one of the following sets is a parametrization of the curve $y=2x-3$, $x\ge0$.
hints: The parametrization must give the right line and exactly the right range of $x$.
For each choice check that $y=2x-3$ holds, then find the range of $x$ produced by the allowed $t$.
A parametrization of a restricted curve must satisfy the equation and have $x$-range equal to the stated restriction.
steps: Each choice satisfies $y=2x-3$, so compare the ranges of $x$.
$x=t+1$ with all real $t$ gives all real $x$; $x=t,\ t\ge1$ gives only $x\ge1$.
$x=\dfrac{t+3}{2},\ t\ge0$ gives $x\ge\dfrac32$; $x=\sin t$ gives only $-1\le x\le1$.

qs.q: The area of the region in the common interior of the polar curves $r=1+\cos\theta$ and $r=1-\cos\theta$ is equal to
hints: This is the area between polar curves; use symmetry.
Find where the curves meet, then take one quadrant's piece and multiply by 4.
$A=\dfrac12\int_\alpha^\beta r^2\,d\theta$, and $\cos^2\theta=\dfrac{1+\cos2\theta}{2}$.
steps: Intersections: $1+\cos\theta=1-\cos\theta$ gives $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ (and $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$). By symmetry the area is 4 times the first-quadrant part, where $r=1-\cos\theta$ is the inner curve.

qs.q: If the area of the triangle with the vertices $A(1,2,0)$, $B(0,0,x)$, and $C(0,-1,0)$ is $3$, then $2x^2=$
hints: The area of a triangle in space comes from a cross product.
Form two edge vectors from a common vertex, compute their cross product, and set half its length equal to the area.
Area of the triangle $=\dfrac12\|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\|$.

qs.q: If the point $R\left(\dfrac{12}{5},2,\dfrac{11}{5}\right)$ lies three-fifths of the way from the point $P(0,5,1)$ to the point $Q(a,b,c)$, then $ac+b=$
hints: Use the vector relation between $\overrightarrow{PR}$ and $\overrightarrow{PQ}$.
Write the relation componentwise and solve for $a$, $b$, $c$.
If $R$ lies a fraction $k$ of the way from $P$ to $Q$, then $\overrightarrow{PR}=k\,\overrightarrow{PQ}$.

qs.q: The area of the region inside the circle $r=2\cos\theta$ and outside both circles $r=2\sin\theta$ and $r=1$ is equal to
hints: This is an area between several polar curves; sketch the three circles and find their intersections.
Find the intersections of the first circle with each of the others and split the region by outer-minus-inner curve.
$A=\dfrac12\int_\alpha^\beta\left(r_{\text{outer}}^2-r_{\text{inner}}^2\right)d\theta$.
